audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is untouched template — every phase why is the generic Galio boilerplate, and the only Heimerdinger-specific noun in it is 'CH-2 Grenade'. The content layer also never says why his zone beats you, only that it does.
audit.why: This lane is a range problem, not a cooldown problem: Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 and the grenade 970, against Winds of War at 825 and Justice Punch at 650. He simply out-ranges every tool you have until you are on top of him.
audit.corrected: Range asymmetry written into the early stages of both layers; the full layer's phase text now describes the turret wall and the rocket range instead of generic Q-poke lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: UPGRADE!!! is never mentioned in either layer — the full layer literally says 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: UPGRADE!!! is 100/85/70 and empowers his next spell, so his level-6 spike is an empowered grenade or turret, not a new ability. That is what makes his 6 dangerous even though his own R deals no damage on its own.
audit.corrected: UPGRADE!!! named at the level-6 phase and in the late-game why with its 100s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions were missing or wrong. (a) The page treats CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade as if the whole area stuns. (b) It never explains why Justice Punch gets through the turret line. (c) It implies clearing turrets buys time. It also claims his grenade 'catches you mid-dash', which the kit does not support.
audit.why: Riot's grenade text: it deals damage in an area 'as well as stunning anyone directly hit and slowing surrounding units' — only the direct hit stuns, the rest is a slow, so the dodge target is the centre of the throw. Justice Punch 'knock[s] up the first enemy CHAMPION he encounters', so turrets and minions do not stop it — that is the mechanism behind the advice already on the page. And H-28 G Evolution Turret is a 1-second, 20-mana cooldown, so a killed turret is replaced immediately; the nest is not a resource you can grind down.
audit.corrected: Direct-hit-only stun, the champion-only Justice Punch collision and the 1s turret redeploy are now stated in both layers; the unsupported mid-dash claim was removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track CH-2 Grenade' appears throughout with no cooldown.
audit.why: The grenade is a flat 11 seconds at every rank — it never gets shorter, which makes it the most reliably punishable cooldown in the lane and is worth saying plainly. Micro-Rockets are 11/10/9/8/7.
audit.corrected: Flat 11s written into the cooldown block, the do's line, Key Ability Interactions, trading rules and the loading tip.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page explains why ganking Heimerdinger is harder than it looks.
audit.why: Hextech Affinity grants him Move Speed near allied towers and his own turrets, so he kites faster inside his nest than outside it. That changes where a gank has to start.
audit.corrected: Written into the level-6 spike and the foe-wants line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer grades this TRICKY at 7.5/10 difficulty.
audit.why: MC_WR_TABLES has Galio at 53.12% over 1271-scale sample (256 games) here, and the content layer's own prose says Galio is favoured from level 3 onward. A 7.5/10 difficulty label on a winning matchup misleads.
audit.corrected: Not changed. diff is 'TRICKY' (6 chars) and no 6-character replacement token exists, so any label change would fail the length check while leaving diffRating inconsistent. Flagged for the user instead.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is his — his first H-28G turret walls you off the minions and chips you while you only have Q poke and no engage, so don't force it and don't step into E-grenade stun range. The saving grace is that everything he throws is magic: channel Shield of Durand through a rocket volley and the amplified reduction makes his poke laughable. At 3, with Q-W-E up, you get your first real window — Justice-Punch THROUGH the turret line to knock him up, release W to taunt him off his minions, and drop your Q tornado on top.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is his — the first H-28 G turret walls you off the minions and his Micro-Rockets reach 1325 against your 825 Winds of War, so you can only avoid the poke, not answer it. Do not step onto the centre of a CH-2 grenade: a direct hit stuns, the splash only slows. The saving grace is that everything he throws is magic, so charging Shield of Durand through a rocket volley makes the reduction laugh at it. At 3, Justice Punch collides with champions, not turrets, so it flies past the line and knocks him up; release W to taunt him off his minions.

edits.before: This is where Galio's anti-mage identity takes over. His entire threat is magic burst — W rockets, turret beams, E grenade — and Shield of Durand's magic-amplified reduction shrugs all of it while the release taunts him. The one thing to dodge is the E stun-grenade: eat that and the turrets melt you before your channel ramps. Bait it, then E in. At 6 your Hero's Entrance flags behind his turret zone and drops you on top of him with a landing knock-up and taunt; his burst commitment just feeds the sponge.
edits.after: This is where Galio's anti-mage identity takes over. His entire threat is magic — Micro-Rockets, turret beams, the CH-2 grenade — and Shield of Durand's magic-amplified reduction shrugs all of it while the release taunts him. The one thing to dodge is a direct grenade hit, because only that stuns; eat it and the turrets melt you before your channel ramps. It is a flat 11s at every rank, so bait it and punch in. At 6 Hero's Entrance drops you on him inside the nest with a landing knockup and taunt.

edits.before: You stay favoured because his damage never stops being magic — your tank-AP build plus Shield of Durand keeps eating his poke long after lane. Heimer becomes a turret-fort splitpush and zone problem, not a 1v1 threat, so your real value is Hero's Entrance rotating to other lanes and fights where you flag in and flash-taunt him off his backline turret nest. Don't try to out-DPS the turrets straight-up — engage on top of him, taunt with the W release, and let your team clean up while his zone is wasted.
edits.after: You stay favoured because his damage never stops being magic — tank-AP plus Shield of Durand keeps eating his poke long after lane. Heimer becomes a turret fort and a zone problem rather than a 1v1 threat, and UPGRADE!!! (100s) turns one grenade or turret into a fight-ender, so never siege the nest head-on. Your value is Hero's Entrance rotating to other lanes and fights, flagging in and flash-taunting him off his backline. Don't out-DPS turrets he redeploys every second — land on top of him, taunt, and let your team clean up.

notes: Best new fact for this page: Justice Punch knocks up 'the first enemy CHAMPION he encounters', so the turret wall does not stop it — the page already advised punching through the line without ever giving the reason, and now it does. Second: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stuns only a direct hit and merely slows the surrounding area, and it is a flat 11s at every rank. Third: H-28 G turrets redeploy on a 1-second cooldown, so grinding the nest down is not a plan. UPGRADE!!! was absent from both layers entirely. Two things I could not fix inside the length rule: (a) the level chart reads Skill/Heimerdinger/Heimerdinger/Skill/Skill/Heimerdinger/Heimerdinger — the identical template shape that galio-vs-gragas and galio-vs-gwen also carry — while the on-disk win rate is 53.12% for Galio over 256 games and the prose says Galio is favoured from 3; 'Heimerdinger' (12 chars) cannot become 'Galio' (5) inside +/-10%. (b) diff 'TRICKY' with diffRating 7.5/10 on a 53% matchup; no 6-character diff token exists to swap in, and changing only the number would leave the label wrong. Both raised in questionsForUser. Packet lists 61.29% over 31 games for this matchup; the on-disk table says 53.12% over 256 — I used the on-disk figure.
